### Say It Well
Author: Pastor Chuck Swindoll
Site: Insight for Living
URL: https://insight.org/resources/daily-devotional/say-it-well?ga=testimonial-resources
Passage: Acts 17:22-31
Points:
- Paul faced the intellectual elite of Athens without intimidation or compromise.
- He began with a courteous observation and used the altar to an unknown god as an entry point.
- He clearly proclaimed the Creator who needs nothing and gives life to all people.
- He connected directly with his audience by quoting their own poets regarding divine origin.
- He concluded unhesitatingly with God's command to repent, anchored in Jesus's resurrection.
- Believers today should communicate Christ's message with careful thought, clarity, and excellence.

### Day 261: Acts 17:15–23
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-261-acts-17-1523.html
Passage: Acts 17:15-23
Points:
- Paul faced the intellectual city of Athens alone while waiting for his companions.
- Deeply grieved by the rampant idolatry, he actively engaged listeners each day in the marketplace.
- When brought before the Areopagus, he showed keen sensitivity to his hearers' cultural context.
- He seized upon their inscription to an unknown god to introduce the living Creator.
- Effective evangelism builds bridges to reach people with the gospel right where they are.
